====================================================================================================

Explainer: What is driving the rapid thaw in U.S.-Syria relations?
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
16:08:11 CST
17:08:11 KST

by Hummam Sheikh Ali
DAMASCUS, Aug. 26 (Xinhua) -- Washington's formal removal of Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism has marked another milestone in a striking transformation of relations between Washington and Damascus, less than two years after the fall of the former Syrian government.
The decision, formally announced Monday, ended a designation that had been in place since 1979 and removed a separate layer of U.S. restrictions that remained even after Washington dismantled much of its broader sanctions architecture against Syria last year.
Analysts say the decision reflects Washington's changing geopolitical calculations in the Middle East, not least prompted by Syria's strategic position and altered regional alliances following the fall of Bashar al-Assad's government in December 2024.
But while the removal of sanctions and other restrictions offers Syria a greater opportunity to reconnect with the international financial system and attract reconstruction investment, experts caution that sanctions relief alone will not resolve the profound economic and institutional challenges left by years of conflict.
FROM ISOLATION TO ENGAGEMENT
The removal of Syria from the State Sponsors of Terrorism list did not, by itself, dismantle the bulk of U.S. economic sanctions against the country. Most broad U.S. sanctions had already been removed through a series of steps beginning in 2025.
In May 2025, the United States authorized transactions that had previously been prohibited under the Syrian Sanctions Regulations, followed by an executive order issued by U.S. President Donald Trump on June 30 terminating the national emergency underlying the Syria sanctions program and revoking six executive orders that formed its foundation.
In August 2025, Washington further relaxed export controls, allowing U.S.-origin goods, software and technology intended purely for civilian use, as well as consumer communications devices and certain civil aviation items, to generally be exported to Syria without individual licenses.
The United States also adopted more favorable licensing treatment for exports related to telecommunications infrastructure, sanitation, electricity generation and civil aviation, while maintaining tighter controls on sensitive dual-use goods and problematic end users.
Syria's designation as a state sponsor of terrorism, however, remained in place until Monday. Its removal means Syria is no longer subject to restrictions specifically arising from that designation, including prohibitions under U.S. terrorism-list sanctions regulations.
Washington simultaneously revoked the designation of al-Nusrah Front, also known as Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham, as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist organization, while the Treasury removed the group from its sanctions list.
For Syria, therefore, Monday's decision represents not the beginning of U.S. sanctions relief, but another major step in a broader dismantling of the legal and political architecture that had isolated Damascus from Washington for decades.
WHY IS WASHINGTON RE-ENGAGING DAMASCUS?
Analysts see the policy shift as driven by considerations extending well beyond bilateral relations.
Mohammad Nader al-Omari, a researcher specializing in international relations and conflict management, told Xinhua that the fall of the former government presented Washington with a geostrategic opportunity to reshape Syria's regional orientation after decades of close relations with Russia and Iran.
He said Syria's geographic position gives it particular importance in U.S. calculations toward several regional and international competitors.
He also pointed to Washington's interest in creating conditions for a security or peace arrangement between Syria and Israel and protecting broader U.S. economic and strategic interests in the region.
These considerations, al-Omari said, have given Syria greater importance in Washington's regional strategy, though its position remains fluid because the country continues to face internal challenges while also sitting at the intersection of competing regional interests, particularly those of Türkiye and Israel.
Syrian writer and journalist Ali Youssef noted that Israeli security and Washington's effort to disrupt military supply routes used by Iran and its regional allies are central to the U.S. approach toward the new Syrian authorities.
The speed of the U.S. policy shift is notable. Relations that were defined for decades by sanctions and confrontation have increasingly moved toward direct engagement, economic opening and cooperation on regional security issues.
CAN POLITICAL OPENING DELIVER ECONOMIC RECOVERY?
For Damascus, one of the most consequential questions is whether political normalization with Washington can translate into investment and reconstruction.
Previously, international banks and companies often avoided the Syrian market because of sanctions-related restrictions as well as legal, regulatory and procedural risks. Removing sanctions-related barriers could give investors greater confidence in considering projects in Syria and boost its reintegration into the international economic system, said al-Omari.
That is particularly important for a country facing enormous reconstruction needs after years of conflict that have damaged housing, electricity networks, transport infrastructure, factories and public services.
But al-Omari cautioned against equating sanctions relief with economic recovery.
"Removing sanctions and designations alone is not enough to make Syria an attractive environment for investment," he said, noting that potential investors will also assess transparency and governance, security, judicial independence, the banking system, investment legislation and property protections.
Likewise, Youssef said improved access to international banking could encourage investors interested in Syrian reconstruction, but argued that security conditions would remain decisive in determining whether capital actually enters the country.
He identified infrastructure, electricity and water networks as areas requiring particular attention, while stressing the importance of strengthening domestic economic activity and reviving agriculture.
The distinction is increasingly important as Damascus seeks to convert diplomatic breakthroughs into tangible economic gains.
For al-Omari, the latest U.S. decision gives the Syrian economy a wider opening to the outside world, but does not guarantee that the opportunity will translate into actual investment.
The scale of its economic impact, he said, will ultimately depend on the Syrian government's ability to carry forward domestic reforms, improve its legal and institutional environment, and establish greater political and security stability. ■

Western countries hosting largest number of Ukrainian refugees significantly cut their aid
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
08:07:07 UTC
17:07:07 KST

MOSCOW, August 26. /TASS/. Germany, Poland, and the Czech Republic, which have taken in the largest number of Ukrainian refugees, significantly reduced their support, according to Eurostat data reviewed by TASS.
Germany currently hosts the largest number of Ukrainian refugees in the EU at 29.2%, amounting to 1.29 million people. Poland houses 961,000 Ukrainian refugees, while the Czech Republic has 381,000.
Since April, Ukrainian citizens applying for temporary protection status in Germany for the first time no longer receive the same assistance package as those who arrived earlier. Social assistance for this group is now distributed according to the general rules for asylum seekers. When deciding whether to grant such assistance, the income and assets of new arrivals are assessed. In mid-2026, Germany transitioned to a new system of basic assistance for refugees. Under this system, applicants' income, savings, and employment status are taken into account.
In March 2026, Poland's 2022 law supporting Ukrainian refugees expired, and new rules took effect, placing Ukrainians under temporary protection on an equal footing with refugees from other countries. Specifically, their cash benefits, free medical care, compensation for housing costs, and access to free education were cut.
As early as 2024, the Czech Republic reduced the period during which Ukrainian refugees could stay in free temporary housing from 150 to 90 days. Once this period expires, new arrivals must find and pay for housing on their own. However, the government continues to provide benefits to socially vulnerable individuals and has maintained payments for the first five months of stay.

Committee chair writes to social media platforms over dangerous driving content
A group of MPs have asked TikTok, Snapchat and other social media companies to explain how they identify dangerous driving content and how many they have removed in the past year, PA reports.
It came after five young people died on Saturday when a Volkswagen Passat, pursued by police, was driven the wrong way down a dual carriageway near Middlesbrough and collided with a police car, killing two officers.
Cleveland police said there was currently “no evidence to indicate that filming of the activities that took place on Friday night and Saturday morning has taken place for the purposes of TikTok”.
However, a social media account thought to have belonged to one of the five people travelling in the Volkswagen shared videos last year appearing to show dangerous driving, the BBC reported.
Caroline Dinenage, who chairs the culture, media and sport committee, said it was “shocking that videos glorifying dangerous driving can be accessed so easily online”.
In her letters to social media companies, including YouTube and Meta – which owns Instagram and Facebook – she said recent reporting on “tragic” road crashes in the UK and Ireland “has brought renewed attention to concerns about content on video-sharing platforms that promotes dangerous driving”.
She has given the platforms until 3 September to respond. TikTok has previously said its policies strictly prohibit content that could cause significant physical harm, including dangerous driving, and that it actively removes any videos and accounts that break its rules.
Meta has also previously said it prohibits people from promoting, advocating for or encouraging participation in so-called high-risk viral challenges, including the trend of dangerous driving against oncoming traffic, adding that it removes such content once it becomes aware of it.
YouTube and Snapchat have been contacted by PA for comment.
Dozens of civil society groups have demanded the UK government do more to promote cycling and walking, after this summer’s extreme heat exposed the desperate need to decarbonise transport.
This summer’s heatwaves and wildfires were “immediate, real-world manifestations of the climate emergency”, the groups said, making reform of transport – responsible for more carbon emissions than any other sector in the UK – an urgent priority.
Last year, domestic transport was responsible for almost a third of the UK’s net greenhouse gas emissions – with the total emissions from the sector increasing 2% over the previous year.
The groups call for a “modal shift” in transport provision. “What that means is creating the conditions which allow people to travel for a higher proportion of the trip by walking, cycling, public transport and shared mobility than by private cars,” said Ben Plowden, the chief executive of the Campaign for Better Transport.
The demand comes after Labour appeared to have shelved targets for an increase in trips made by public transport and a reduction in trips using private vehicles.

Labour’s energy bills crisis is getting worse. Political honesty is essential
Nils Pratley
Another Ofgem energy price cap day, another increase in bills. Miatta Fahnbulleh, the new energy secretary, can blame the usual culprit on Wednesday – the fossil fuel price “rollercoaster”, given a shove this time by Donald Trump’s Middle East misadventure. Higher gas prices will indeed be the main quarter-on-quarter reason why bills stand at a three-year high on a unit basis, writes our financial editor Nils Pratley.
But there is more to the tale on a longer view. Even when the gas rollercoaster dips downwards, the energy industry’s medium-term projections suggest bills will not fall meaningfully.
Look at the forecast on Tuesday from EDF, one of the big retail suppliers, assuming “some moderation” in wholesale prices. Top line: “Bills still look stubbornly high at the end of the decade.” Versus its assumed £1,721 for the price cap for the last three months of 2026, the company projects £1,786 in 2030.
The number would be £90 lower if the government extends VAT relief on electricity and continues to take a portion of older green levies into general taxation. Either way, former energy secretary Ed Miliband’s naive, or cynical, “£300 off bills by 2030” promise looks non-operative at this point.
As the prime minister calls on businesses to offer work experience opportunities for young people, a survey has found more than one in three employers have reduced the number of entry-level jobs in the past year.
A Survation survey of 1,001 UK senior business leaders, commissioned by the Work Foundation thinktank at Lancaster University, found 36% reduced entry-level jobs for 16 to 24 years olds over the past 12 months, while almost half of medium-sized (48%) and large employers (46%) reported cuts, compared with 24% of small employers.
Ben Harrison, director of the Work Foundation at Lancaster University, said:
Young people are entering one of the toughest labour markets in years, facing intense competition for a shrinking number of entry-level jobs and fewer opportunities to get a secure foothold in work.
Our research suggests the challenge is not simply how to provide young people with more employment support. Opportunities for young people are declining, and for those living in weaker local labour markets, the options they face are constrained.
But that doesn’t mean government should step back from its drive to improve job security and pay – both of which will be key in reducing youth unemployment over the long term. The focus must remain on boosting the quality and quantity of roles available to young people. And that means doing more to directly create good jobs, while also providing additional support to employers to do likewise.”

MINSK, 26 August (BelTA) - Belarusian farmers have threshed 8.7 million tonnes of grain, BelTA learned from the press service of the Belarusian Agriculture and Food Ministry.
 
As of 26 August 2026, grain harvest including rapeseed amounted to 8.713 million tonnes. By region, the progress in the harvest looks as follows: Minsk Oblast – 2,347,000 tonnes, Grodno Oblast – 1,771,000 tonnes, Brest Oblast – 1,637,000 tonnes, Mogilev Oblast – 1,074,000 tonnes, Gomel Oblast – 1,054,000 tonnes, Vitebsk Oblast – 830,000 tonnes.
 
Grain and leguminous crops (including rapeseed, without corn) have been harvested from 2,360,000 hectares or 95% of the areas (2,432,000 hectares in total).
 
Deliveries under the state procurement order include: 585,000 tonnes of food grain (88% of the target); and 82,000 tonnes of malting barley (95% of the 86,000-tonne target).
 
Second cut was harvested across an area of 874,000 hectares or 86% of the plan. 
 
Hay production has reached 538,000 tonnes or 75% of the plan. Silage harvest progress stands at 795,000 tonnes. Forage grasses total 3,830,000 tonnes or 38% of the target. Haylage production has reached 11,906,000 tonnes, or 83% of the target. 
 
Fertilizer stocks (nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium) for winter planting have been procured at 147% (253,000 tonnes) of the planned requirement.

Special operation &quot;Rubicon&quot; exposed drug network with more than 360 suspects - drugs, property and money worth half a billion found
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
11:02:47 EEST
17:02:47 KST

Special operation "Rubicon" exposed drug network with more than 360 suspects - drugs, property and money worth half a billion found
Kyiv • UNN
They conducted 1,209 searches and seized more than one tonne of drugs and 22 tonnes of precursors. The total value of the seized items exceeded UAH 540 million\r\n.
As part of the international special operation "Rubicon" to expose the drug trade, 1,209 searches were conducted, 367 suspects, 42 drug laboratories and 138 warehouses were uncovered, and more than a tonne of finished drugs, 50 cars and approximately a quarter of a million dollars in various currencies were seized, the Office of the Prosecutor General reported on Wednesday, UNN writes.
Details
"A large-scale international special operation, "Rubicon," aimed at eliminating the transnational system of industrial production and sale of drugs and psychotropic substances has been completed," the statement said.
Joint investigative and operational measures by law enforcement agencies of Ukraine, Poland and Moldova have been ongoing since February this year with the participation of Europol.
According to the investigation, the network covered the full cycle of the drug business—from the smuggling of precursors and production of psychotropic substances to their storage, logistics, online distribution and legalization of funds.
According to the Prosecutor's Office, "precursors were smuggled from EU countries to Ukraine and Poland. In clandestine laboratories, they were used to produce α-PVP, amphetamine, mephedrone and other psychotropic substances. The laboratories were set up in rented private houses, dacha cooperatives, garages and abandoned industrial premises."
"Finished drugs were packaged in clandestine warehouses, sent through postal services and distributed by 'dead-drop couriers.' Sales were conducted through more than 130 anonymous platforms in messengers and chatbots. Payments were mainly made in cryptocurrency," the Office of the Prosecutor General noted.
The special operation, as stated, took place in three stages. Law enforcement officers shut down drug laboratories and warehouses, blocked cross-border channels for the supply of precursors, documented more than 100 controlled purchases, and identified senders, administrators of online stores and drug storage locations. At the final stage, the remaining cells of the network were dismantled and its members detained.
Following the three stages in Ukraine:
-  1,209 searches were conducted; 
-  367 people were notified of suspicion; 
-  42 drug laboratories were dismantled; 
-  the operation of 138 warehouses containing finished drug products was stopped; 
-  56 drug shops were exposed. 
"More than a tonne of finished drug products and 22 tonnes of precursors were seized from illegal circulation; according to preliminary estimates, they could have been used to produce more than 4 tonnes of drugs. Also seized were 50 cars, UAH 1.6 million, USD 167,000 and EUR 39,000. The total value of the seized items at 'black market' prices exceeds UAH 540 million," the Office of the Prosecutor General reported.
According to preliminary estimates, the seized drug products and raw materials represent several million potential doses that did not enter illegal circulation.

US owes full compensation for damages caused by unilateral sanctions, Iran says
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
21:21:46 UTC
06:21:46 KST

Iran has said that the US bears international responsibility for damages caused by its unilateral sanctions and must provide full compensation, including restitution and reparations.
In a message to the UN and Security Council, Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi described the US measures as an “economic terrorism campaign” carried out through unilateral coercive measures, which he said are unlawful under international law.
“The Islamic Republic of Iran reserves its right to resort to all available means to pursue accountability, compensation and redress, and to hold the perpetrators of these inhumane and unlawful acts accountable,” Araghchi said, according to Iran’s state broadcaster IRIB.
He said the US campaign “entails international responsibility, including an obligation to provide full compensation for all material and moral damages, including restitution and reparations, in accordance with international law.”
Araghchi also said the US bears “full international responsibility” and can face individual criminal responsibility, if the relevant legal elements are established, for the consequences of “unlawful and criminal acts and the harm caused to the Iranian people.”
He urged the UN Security Council and member states to condemn and reject Washington’s use of “unilateral coercive measures and secondary sanctions” to pressure sovereign states into changing their legitimate economic interests and trade relations.
Iran also called on countries not to recognise, approve or implement such measures that seek to link their sovereign rights to policies unilaterally determined by Washington.
Araghchi urged the US “to immediately halt threats and coercive actions aimed at forcing third countries and their nationals to alter legitimate economic relations and interests.”
He also called on the UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres to assess and report on the humanitarian and human rights consequences of such measures, including their impact on civilians’ access to food, medicine, health care, energy, transportation and humanitarian assistance.
Araghchi said relevant evidence should be independently assessed, documented and preserved to ensure future accountability.
“Operation Economic Outcast”
On Monday, the Trump administration launched “Operation Economic Outcast,” a sweeping sanctions campaign aimed at further isolating Iran from the global financial system.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the measures target key Iranian economic sectors, including aviation, shipping, gold, technology and digital assets, with more than 60 entities, individuals and vessels blacklisted.
Bessent said Washington’s objective was to sever Iran’s economic lifelines, describing the campaign as the “economic asphyxiation” of the Iranian government.
Last week, US President Donald Trump announced his intention to launch what he called “the most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country,” describing his maximum-pressure campaign against Iran as “economic warfare and isolation on an unprecedented scale.”
He also said countries that provide Tehran with an economic “lifeline” – through their financial institutions, businesses, airports, or government entities – would face severe economic consequences.
The US and Israel launched attacks on Iran in late February, prompting Tehran to retaliate against Israel and US military assets across the region before a ceasefire agreement was reached in April.
In mid-June, Washington and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding calling for freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, but implementation of the deal later stalled amid persistent differences.
Last month, the US resumed its attacks on Iran, while Tehran responded by targeting US military facilities and equipment in a number of Arab countries.

Bill Gates warned about the risks of the rapid development of artificial intelligence
Kyiv • UNN
Bill Gates said that AI is developing faster than governments and society are prepared for. He called for reforms to policy and taxation.
Bill Gates said that artificial intelligence is developing faster than governments and society are preparing for its consequences. He warned about changes in the labor market, cyber and biological risks, and problems with controlling the technology. This is reported by Axios, according to UNN.
Details
According to the publication, in a new memo, Bill Gates noted that AI could significantly change both white-collar and blue-collar jobs. In particular, he said that the changes could affect law, medicine, software, customer service, and manufacturing.
Artificial intelligence will either be the greatest fictional equalizer or the worst source of inequality
According to him, without additional measures, there could be significantly fewer new jobs than there are today. Bill Gates believes that governments need new institutions to coordinate policy in the areas of security, employment, education, taxation, and healthcare. He also proposes considering taxation of the use of AI and robots.
At the current course and speed, there is a very high likelihood of a net negative outcome
At the same time, Gates acknowledged that coordinating global action would be difficult. According to him, representatives of technology companies and laboratories are also concerned about the speed of AI development.
Recall
Generative AI creates new content based on data, unlike traditional AI, which only analyzes it. It accelerates content creation and reduces costs, but requires verification of the generated information.

Brain-tech push gains pace as China draws up standards and firms challenge Neuralink
Unknown
Unknown Publisher

Brain-tech push gains pace as China draws up standards and firms challenge Neuralink
Dozens of guidelines are coming, covering medical, industrial and consumer users as emerging neural technology moves towards wider adoption
China is drawing up an extensive set of standards for brain-computer interface technology, seeking to accelerate the commercialisation of a field in which Chinese start-ups are increasingly competing with Elon Musk’s Neuralink for global leadership.
Under draft guidelines released by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT), Beijing aims to formulate or revise more than 40 standards by 2028 and encourage at least 100 companies to adopt them. It also plans to lead or participate in the development of more than 10 international standards.
By 2030, China aims to have developed more than 80 standards, creating a comprehensive framework for the domestic industry while increasing its influence over global rules for the emerging neural technology.
Brain-computer interfaces allow the mind to communicate directly with external devices. Their potential uses range from restoring movement and speech in people with disabilities to controlling computers, industrial machinery and consumer electronics.
Domestically, China has leading neural-tech firms such as Neuracle, which has won approval for an implanted system that helps paralysed patients regain hand movement, as well as StairMed and NeuroXess, which focus on invasive implants and the interpretation of neural signals, and BrainCo, which develops non-invasive devices and brain-controlled prosthetics.

‘You have to smell that bread to understand’: Lukashenko’s philosophy on food security
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
08:00:00 UTC
17:00:00 KST

Autumn is just around the corner. Soon many will be taking stock of the summer, reminiscing about moments from their travels, and compiling photo albums of their vacations. For farmers, however, it will be time to calculate grain yields and tally the total weight of the 2026 harvest. For them, summer is not a vacation season, but the peak of intense work. They greet the sunrise at work and watch the sunset there too; they see a sea of work ahead and harvest tonnes of grain. The harvest campaign is the key news topic of every summer and the main subject of discussion for all Belarusians,  from machine operators to the president. For the head of state, working in the fields during the harvest season is a given. Out in the field, one can assess the performance of machinery and talk with the people who work the land. Field conditions are no obstacle to discussing matters of national importance. In the How It Was project, we will explore how Aleksandr Lukashenko, while monitoring the progress of the harvest, takes stock of the development across various sectors.
Why is it important for the president to work in the fields?
Belarus is no longer fighting for the harvest. Today, the country has everything it needs to carry out the campaign calmly and methodically, with a steady work rhythm. But the strategy and mindset remain martial: no stepping back, only forward. It is no coincidence that the harvest season is kept under the president’s close watch every year. The reason goes beyond Aleksandr Lukashenko’s personal attachment to the land; first and foremost, it is a matter of state importance. 
“When you don't have your own and someone else supplies it to you, they can grab you by the throat at any moment. And that’s it. No independence, no sovereignty. What’s more, a whole chain of industry rests on domestic agriculture, from ploughs to super-harvesters. Your own agriculture means schools, traditions, and an entire way of life. Truth is, if you’ve never breathed in the aroma of that bread, you'll never understand why we have to have our own. We’ve got to have our own in everything we're capable of! That’s what takes us further, lifts the nation, and gives people the chance to earn a living,” the president said as he inspected the harvest in the fields 1st Minsk Poultry Farm in 2018.
Aleksandr Lukashenko inspects the harvest progress in the fields of 1st Minsk Poultry Farm, August 2018
The president, in fact, has a number of compelling arguments as to why the harvesting campaign is about more than just agriculture. “We must remember that one farmer provides work for seven or eight people. Think about it: grain first has to be grown, then milled, then baked into bread or used to feed poultry. If we were to stop all that, just imagine - half the country would be out of work,” the head of state said during a conversation with journalists in the field at 1st Minsk Poultry Farm. 
In 2018, during a national seminar on rural development and improving the efficiency of the agricultural sector, the president stated that agricultural production had long since ceased to be viewed solely as a part of the economy: “Food is politics, both domestic and foreign. That’s why, from the very dawn of our independence, making an emphasis on a strong agricultural sector as one of the country’s development priorities was the right call. No one argues with that anymore. The well-being and social and political stability of the country depend to a large extent on the state of the agricultural industry. Just imagine, if we didn’t have our own food and clothing, what kind of independence would we have? Where would we be today, and before whom would we be kneeling?”
Aleksandr Lukashenko addresses a national seminar on rural development and improving the efficiency of the agricultural sector, April 2018 
How industrialists fulfilled the president’s dream 
Back in Soviet times, there was a clear division of labor in the production of agricultural machinery: Rostselmash manufactured grain harvesters, Gomselmash produced forage harvesters. After the collapse of the USSR, Belarus saw a sharp decline in its fleet of grain harvesters due to equipment wear and tear. By 1995, the country had about 22,500 of them, 7,800 fewer than in 1990. New machinery had to be purchased, but young, sovereign Belarus simply did not have the money. Necessity, as they say, is the mother of invention and it pushed Belarusian specialists toward import substitution.
In March 1996, the president visited Gomselmash. The plant’s specialists presented the head of state with a feasibility study for the development of Belarus’ first grain harvester. The idea received his backing, and financial support. By August 1996, Aleksandr Lukashenko took a test drive in the first Belarusian grain harvesting complex - the KZR‑10 Polesye‑Rotor. The president was clearly pleased with the test drive. With the green light from the top, the Gomselmash team began working intensively on new models of grain harvesters. What emerged was not just a line-up of machinery, but an entire school of engineering excellence.

If we were to stop all that, just imagine - half the country would be out of work,” the head of state said during a conversation with journalists in the field at 1st Minsk Poultry Farm.

That’s why, from the very dawn of our independence, making an emphasis on a strong agricultural sector as one of the country’s development priorities was the right call. Just imagine, if we didn’t have our own food and clothing, what kind of independence would we have? Where would we be today, and before whom would we be kneeling?”
Aleksandr Lukashenko addresses a national seminar on rural development and improving the efficiency of the agricultural sector, April 2018
How industrialists fulfilled the president’s dream
Back in Soviet times, there was a clear division of labor in the production of agricultural machinery: Rostselmash manufactured grain harvesters, Gomselmash produced forage harvesters. After the collapse of the USSR, Belarus saw a sharp decline in its fleet of grain harvesters due to equipment wear and tear. By 1995, the country had about 22,500 of them, 7,800 fewer than in 1990. New machinery had to be purchased, but young, sovereign Belarus simply did not have the money. Necessity, as they say, is the mother of invention and it pushed Belarusian specialists toward import substitution.
In March 1996, the president visited Gomselmash. The plant’s specialists presented the head of state with a feasibility study for the development of Belarus’ first grain harvester. The idea received his backing, and financial support. By August 1996, Aleksandr Lukashenko took a test drive in the first Belarusian grain harvesting complex - the KZR‑10 Polesye‑Rotor. The president was clearly pleased with the test drive. With the green light from the top, the Gomselmash team began working intensively on new models of grain harvesters. What emerged was not just a line-up of machinery, but an entire school of engineering excellence.
“Gomselmash has always been, is, and will be in this country,” Aleksandr Lukashenko said in 2019 in Vetka District. “Twenty to twenty-five years ago, people tried to convince me that we didn’t need harvesters, didn’t need anything, and that Gomselmash should be sold. Today we can see that it is a good school. A good group of scientists and designers. This school must not be destroyed. And this machinery is needed. But we must keep moving.”
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Aleksandr Lukashenko visits a field in Vetka District, July 2019 
 
 
 In 2021, Aleksandr Lukashenko and the KZR-10 Polesie-Rotor met again in the field - this time on the fields of the Ostoshitsy farm in Logoisk District. “It’s time to take it out of service and put it on a pedestal - in a museum. That’s where it all began. But looking at it – it’s beautiful, you wouldn’t say it’s old,” the president suggested at the time. He recalled that in 1996 they couldn’t make anything better that quickly, so they settled on this model. It was a decent and, most importantly, budget-friendly harvester that harvested without losses. “I dreamed that we would start making our own harvesters. And that dream has come true,” the Belarusian leader admitted.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 They didn’t stop at just one fulfilled dream. Year after year, the capabilities of Belarusian harvesters have been improved. Aleksandr Lukashenko has kept a close eye on this process. The president consistently motivates manufacturers to increase the level of localization in their machinery and, most importantly, to ensure quality. And he tests new models right in the field. In August 2017, on a wheat field of the Aleksandriyskoye farm in Shklov District, the president was presented with the most productive harvester at that time - the KZS-1624-1 from Gomselmash.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Aleksandr Lukashenko during a visit to a field at the Aleksandriyskoye farm in Shklov District, August 2017 
 
 
 “I want to see how this harvester performs in the field. Because industrialists have a habit of puffing up their cheeks, claiming we have good harvesters, no worse than foreign counterparts. Let’s see how it compares to others,” the Belarusian leader said at the time. After the test drive, he gave his feedback and instructed the team to refine the model. A few days later, at a meeting in the Palace of Independence, the head of state set Gomselmash the task of developing a super-harvester that would surpass imported models. And by August 2018, on the fields of Aleksandriyskoye, the president successfully tested the promised KZS-2124.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Aleksandr Lukashenko during a visit to a field at the Aleksandriyskoye farm in Shklov District, August 2017 
 
 
 In 2025, on the fields of the Ozeritsky-Agro farm, the president was shown the advanced domestic grain harvesters GS12A1 PRO in action. “This is a dream. If it is high-quality – it’s a dream,” the president said at the time.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Aleksandr Lukashenko during a visit to a field at the Ozeritsky-Agro farm, July 2025 
 
 
 An important point: the head of state asks about the features of harvesters not only from designers and plant managers. He always seeks the opinion of machine operators and harvester operators, people who spend almost around the clock with this machinery and know every detail. Their schedule during the harvest is extremely demanding, but a conversation with the president is a welcome break. The head of state often adjusts to the farmers’ schedules. In 2023, the president’s visit to the fields of the Olekshitsy farm in Berestovitsa District coincided with the harvester operators’ lunch break. So the president discussed the pros and cons of the machinery with them over lunch.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Aleksandr Lukashenko visits the Olekshitsy agricultural enterprise, August 2023 
 
 
 However, the friendly attitude toward harvester operators does not diminish strict oversight of machinery maintenance. “We monitor the use of machinery across all areas. But you should also make sure that maintenance is done on time – don’t push the machinery too hard. If you can’t go into the field, don’t go – don’t break it. Because if this tractor breaks down, you will have to spend a quarter of your grain harvest on repairs. Take care of the machinery. It needs to be looked after,” the president warned workers at the Zhuravlinoye farm in Pruzhany District in 2022. Hence a common task for all agricultural enterprises - to approach the organization of machine yards wisely. How can you harvest if the machinery is not in order?
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Aleksandr Lukashenko during a visit to the Zhuravlinoye farm, August 2022 
 
 
 How down-to-earth issues motivate farmers to work more efficiently 
 
 
 The yield of Belarusian grain varieties is often higher than imported ones, so the president’s demand to work with domestic seeds is self-evident. First, it is a matter of responsible management. Second, agricultural science develops in response to real needs, if there are problems with certain varieties, breeders must solve them. In 2014, during a working trip to Minsk District, the president raised the issue of lodging in the fields, asking what measures could help prevent this problem in the future. Among all conditions, the most important factor is the choice of variety. Some varieties, even with good yields, are prone to lodging, which can be worsened by weather conditions. Hence the president’s instruction: pay close attention to crop rotation and use varieties most resistant to lodging. In short, do everything possible to preserve the harvest.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Aleksandr Lukashenko during an inspection of the harvest campaign in Minsk District, July 2014 
 
In 2022, Aleksandr Lukashenko visited the crop breeding and seed production complex of the Scientific and Practical Center of the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus. The center’s specialists engage in crop breeding and the production of original seeds. “'It fills me with pride that we have preserved agricultural science. And not only in seed production. These people are extraordinary! We have both preserved and surpassed [previous achievements]. This is worth more than gold. Bread begins with scientists and these plots,” the Belarusian leader shared his impressions at the time. The achievements of Belarusian scientists are also recognized by their foreign colleagues. For instance, the Belarusian wheat variety Kapylyanka was recognized as unique and placed in the Svalbard Global Seed Vault in the Arctic ice, where the best samples from across the planet are preserved.
The head of state reviews the work of Belarusian scientists both during his visits to agricultural enterprises and on his personal homestead. During a working trip to Logoisk District in 2021, the president spoke about an experiment with watermelons. “I started with one Dutch variety. Yesterday we harvested five different varieties. They brought them to my kitchen so I could sample them, and I picked out the two best ones. The Belarusian variety is already quite good. And back when I started doing this, I said: the time will come when we will be cultivating our own. Today, our watermelon is absolutely no different from the one sent to me by Emomali Rahmon [president of Tajikistan]. Experts say they are actually healthier for us,” Aleksandr Lukashenko said. According to him, exactly the same approach is applied to other crops, such as new potato varieties. “The potatoes developed by our scientists even taste different... I observe what scientists provide to producers,” the Belarusian leader noted.
Aleksandr Lukashenko joins harvest on his homestead, August 2021The land requires a gentle touch. This is something the president knows well, often bringing up soil preparation when visiting the fields. “We have forgotten how to plow. If a field is plowed carelessly and half-heartedly, and we have to level it with a grader, then it is better not to plow at all,” the head of state emphasized on a field in the Starye Dorogi District in 2019. “No seed drill will level it, even a multi-purpose one. I remember that back in my days, the Party demanded that machine operators be paid very well for plowing. Even more than for harvesting. If the field is plowed evenly, the seeding costs are lower.”
Work on the land is always carefully scheduled, so even at the height of the harvest, the sowing season remains a pressing topic. First and foremost, this concerns winter crop planting. The head of state often emphasizes that a truly efficient farmer plows the fields and prepares them for winter planting while simultaneously harvesting the grain. “We started the grain harvest and, frankly speaking, we are dragging our feet with these grains, forgetting that immediately after harvesting the crops, we need to plow and prepare the land for winter sowing, and plant winter crops,” Aleksandr Lukashenko said during his visit to the Ozeritsky-Agro enterprise in Smolevichi District in 2019.
How the land feeds Belarus 
The president always sets challenging tasks for farmers and immediately reveals the secret to achieving them: iron discipline and technology. Farming culture and technological discipline help agricultural workers master a wide variety of crops. For instance, the head of state has repeatedly highlighted the advantages of winter barley. One of the benefits of cultivating it is an early harvest, which allows machine operators to test the equipment before the mass harvest. Furthermore, this crop serves as an excellent feed base for livestock. Cultivating winter barley is challenging but achievable. “From all perspectives, winter barley must be cultivated. In Soviet times, people took a negligent attitude towards it. Today, the technology, the equipment, and the people are different. We can easily get good barley yields. So, we must be bolder in trying,” the Belarusian leader emphasized during a working trip to Slutsk District in 2022.
 
  
 
 
 
The head of state reviews the work of Belarusian scientists both during his visits to agricultural enterprises and on his personal homestead. During a working trip to Logoisk District in 2021, the president spoke about an experiment with watermelons. “I started with one Dutch variety. Yesterday we harvested five different varieties. They brought them to my kitchen so I could sample them, and I picked out the two best ones. The Belarusian variety is already quite good. And back when I started doing this, I said: the time will come when we will be cultivating our own. So, we must be bolder in trying,” the Belarusian leader emphasized during a working trip to Slutsk District in 2022.
Aleksandr Lukashenko visits Kozlovichi-Agro during a working trip to Slutsk District, July 2022 
 
 
 Aleksandr Lukashenko actively motivates farmers to work with another promising crop for the country – rapeseed. “Rapeseed means money. We need to promote rapeseed oil. Rapeseed is a remedy, especially for us. We export it all over the world, yet we rely on sunflower oil ourselves. We need to buy our own if we want to be healthy,” the president stated on a field in Minsk District in 2020. Today, growing rapeseed is a settled matter. First of all, rapeseed is a very “polite” crop: grains grow excellently in the fields after its cultivation, and agricultural workers call rapeseed a “predecessor crop.” Secondly, rapeseed yields highly beneficial oil and protein for livestock needs. Thirdly, rapeseed represents Belarus’ export potential. During a visit to Smolevichi District in 2025, Aleksandr Lukashenko personally evaluated rapeseed oil and pointed out its health benefits. “It is a very good thing. If you want to be healthy, you need to use this oil. The oil is highly beneficial. In general, I advocate for eating what grows in your own land,” the Belarusian leader said. In 2026, the winter rapeseed harvest hit a record of 1.4 million tonnes. This marks an all-time high for the crop’s cultivation in Belarus, achieving an average yield of 3.2 centners per hectare. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
One should not forget about corn either, the head of state noted. “We will probably keep farming corn. It helps a lot in Gomel Oblast, and across the entire country. Corn means good grain, juicy fodder, and silage,” the Belarusian leader emphasized while working in Petrikov District in 2024. In 2007 Aleksandr Lukashenko declared corn a crop of strategic importance and encouraged to harvest more than a million tonnes of the grain in Belarus. Despite the fact that a year earlier the country had harvested only 150,000 tonnes. The breakthrough has been made, and today the country harvests up to two million tonnes of corn grain. And this work does not stop, Belarusian scientists are working on the production of domestic varieties of corn. But for now there is a difference in comparison with foreign varieties. For example, in terms of ripening the foreign varieties mature sooner, and Belarusian varieties still have inferior yields. However, breeding in this area is making great strides, and the productivity of hybrids has grown significantly. The president personally got acquainted with results of this work in a field of OAO Aleksandriyskoye in 2024. Then the opinion of the head of state was as follows: “Our corn is not bad, what can I say. But we lag behind the West.”
 
 
 
 
 
 Who is responsible for the standard of living in the country? 
 
 
 The matter of the harvesting campaign is of strategic importance for Belarus. During a conference call in 2022 the president explained why this is so important: “We have to provide the population with food, increase our stabilization funds, i.e. reserves for the future. And, as I’ve said, given today’s good food prices, we have to improve the economy of agriculture. Especially since we have everything to achieve these goals.”
 
 
 
 
 
 The most important thing is that to achieve these goals there are people who are not afraid of hard work. And they work selflessly during the harvesting campaign because during the harvest season there are no days off, every day and every hour is precious. The president never forgets the role of agricultural workers in the life of the country and highly appreciates their contribution. For example, not so long ago in order to thank the top performers of the 2026 harvesting campaign, Aleksandr Lukashenko personally went to a field in Minsk District. A small solemn ceremony in field conditions, words of gratitude – and back to work, the main honors will come later.
 
 
 
 
 
 The Dazhynki festival has long become an integral part of the harvesting campaign and a beautiful final note in the great work. In 2024 at the festival in the town of Mosty Aleksandr Lukashenko confessed his love for Dazhynki: “I have a special attitude to this great, kind peasant holiday. Because this is our holiday, kind and most real, the one that life itself has created. This is the result of colossal work and the joy about its results. An occasion to give well-deserved praise to the hands that grow bread and smell like bread.”
 
 
 
 
 
 Aleksandr Lukashenko at a ceremony to honor agrarians during the Dazhynki festival in the town of Mosty, November 2024 
 
 
 Dazhynki is also an important social project. First, it shows to the whole country the real heroes of our time who are not afraid of even the most difficult work. A great career guidance option for training personnel in the countryside. Second, the town that hosts the festival prepares seriously for Dazhynki, infrastructure is renewed, roads are repaired, new facilities are opened. The first republican festival and fair of rural workers Dazhynki took place in Stolin in 1996. And since then, thanks to the holiday of agricultural workers, dozens of small settlements have been noticeably transformed.
 
 
 
 
 
 Social affairs are always on the agenda of the president’s working trips during the harvest season. While talking to Rogachev District residents in 2021, the head of state recalled how 15 years earlier in Belarus they had a thought that “debts to the countryside must be repaid”. Since then programs for the revival of the countryside have been implemented, agrotowns were created, the production sector was developed, and more powerful equipment began to be delivered for the needs of agriculture. And no matter how realities change, the task of preserving the countryside remains unchanged. Because the life of the country, the welfare of our people, foreign exchange earnings, the level of food security and ultimately the social and political stability in the country depend on the state of affairs in the countryside.
 
 
 
 
 
 Aleksandr Lukashenko at a meeting with local residents in the agrotown of Tikhinichi, Rogachev District, August 2021 
 
 
 On the whole, agricultural workers have something to be proud of. Belarus is fully self-sufficient as far as the main types of food are concerned. It significantly exceeds other CIS states’ output of such products and their consumption per capita. And behind this is the huge work of hardworking, responsible and dedicated people. Therefore, the president never spares kind words for agricultural workers: “You are the foundation of our life and the foundation of our security. It is thanks only to you that today we have not been dragged into any wars, confrontations and conflicts. We live a seemingly modest life, but a peaceful one, and this is the key thing,” the president addressed agricultural workers at the oblast Dazhynki festival in Polotsk in 2024. “The rest is in our hands. You are true patriots of your land, having dedicated your lives to the noblest of pursuits – farm work.”
 
 
 
 
 
Aleksandr Lukashenko during a visit to the oblast Dazhynki festival in Polotsk, November 2024

Massive boost for Team Melli as Amini comes back
TEHRAN - Mohammad Amini is all set for a comeback in the international stage as the young star has rejoined Iran mere days before Window 4 of the FIBA Basketball World Cup 2027 Asian Qualifiers.
The Iran basketball federation announced that the development Tuesday, as Team Melli have arrived in the Philippine capital for the August 27-31 games at the Mall of Asia Arena.
Mohammad Amini, an Iranian basketball player and player for the French team Nancy, has joined the national team in Manila, Philippines, to accompany the national team in the fourth window of the 2027 World Cup Qualifiers.
The 21-year-old is expected to be suiting up for the continental powerhouse for the first time since Asia Cup 2025 in Saudi Arabia, where the team gave the country their first medal in the event in eight years by copping bronze.
Back healthier
He was unable to play in their 79-73 victory over New Zealand in the Third-Place Game due to a knee issue he sustained in the Semi-Finals versus Australia, but there was no denying the impact he had in the whole tilt.
Amini averaged 14.6 points and 5.8 rebounds, and his best showing came in the Quarter-Finals when he dropped 30 and 11 to help lead his side to a 78-75 win over Chinese Taipei in a comeback of epic proportions.
Massive boost
If ever, the upcoming window will be his fourth appearance in the senior level. It could be recalled that he made his men's team debut in the World Cup in 2023, then returned for the 2025 Asia Cup Qualifiers.
This time, he's carrying even more experience under his belt. A member of French club SLUC Nancy Basket for four years now, Amini played for the Boston Celtics in the 2026 NBA Summer League last July.
And his return shall make Team Melli even better despite the absence of Sina Vahedi, who continues to tread the road to recovery after suffering an anterior cruciate ligament injury he suffered in the club scene last March.
He's coming in to serve as a mismatch of sorts anew at the backcourt given his 2.01 M (6'7") frame, adding more dynamic to a rotation that already has Sarem Jafari, Mobin Shekhi, and Piter Girgoorian, to name a few, fiba.basketball reported.
Mo through the years
Amini is expected to see action against New Zealand and the Philippines in Window 4, in that order, with Iran, of course, hoping to sustain their fine play after topping Group D with a 5-1 card back in the First Round.

Air defense downs 134 of 162 Russian targets, hits recorded at 18 locations
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
10:55:14 EEST
16:55:14 KST

On the night of Wednesday, the Defense Forces of Ukraine neutralized 134 Russia targets; however, hits were recorded at 18 locations and falling debris at three, reported the Air Force of the Armed Forces of Ukraine.
"According to preliminary data, as of 08:00, air defense shot down/suppressed 134 Russian Shahed-type, Gerbera, and other types of UAVs in the north, south, and east of the country," according to the statement.
In total, on the night of August 26 (from 18:00 on August 25), Russia attacked with 162 Shahed-type strike UAVs (including jet-powered ones), Gerbera, and Parodiya-type decoy drones from the directions of Kursk, Orel, Primorsko-Akhtarsk – Russia, temporarily occupied territories of Donetsk, and Hvardiyske – temporarily occupied territory of the AR of Crimea.
The air attack was repelled by aviation, anti-aircraft missile troops, electronic warfare and unmanned systems units, and mobile fire groups of the Defense Forces of Ukraine.

Ukraine’s president awards Musk Ukraine’s Order of Freedom
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
07:54:17 UTC
16:54:17 KST

- President Zelensky signed a decree on August 26 awarding Elon Musk Ukraine's Order of Freedom for his role in Ukraine-U.S. relations.
- The decree cites Musk's leadership of SpaceX and Tesla, whose Starlink network has supported Ukrainian battlefield communications since 2022.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky signed a decree awarding Elon Musk the Order of Freedom, Ukraine’s highest state honor for foreign nationals, according to Decree No. 835/2026 published August 26.
The decree cites Musk’s “outstanding personal merit in protecting human life and freedom” and his role in developing relations between the peoples of Ukraine and the United States.
The decree identifies Musk as “an entrepreneur, engineer, and head of the companies SpaceX and Tesla” and lists his country as the United States. It does not name Starlink specifically, though the service built by Musk’s company SpaceX has functioned as a central pillar of Ukraine’s wartime defense since Russia’s full-scale invasion began in 2022.
Starlink terminals have given Ukrainian forces reliable, hard-to-jam communications across the front line, connecting units in real time in areas where conventional cell and internet infrastructure has been destroyed or disrupted by Russian strikes. That connectivity has underpinned much of Ukraine’s ability to coordinate troop movements, direct artillery fire and guide drone strikes against Russian positions in occupied territory. Without a resilient satellite link of that kind, Ukrainian commanders would have struggled to maintain coordinated control of forces spread across a front line stretching hundreds of kilometers.
SpaceX has also declined to make Starlink available to Russian forces. The company moved to close a technical loophole that had allowed Russian troops to access the network inside occupied Ukrainian territory, a decision Ukrainian officials have said significantly degraded Russian offensive coordination in the areas affected.
Ukraine’s continued access to Starlink has depended not only on SpaceX but on financial support from partner governments, several of which have funded terminal purchases and service contracts for the Ukrainian military since the early stages of the war.
Zelensky signed a series of other state honor decrees around the same period in August, awarding the Order of Freedom to the leaders of Norway, Finland, Lithuania, Sweden and Estonia on August 21, alongside a newly created distinction called “Gratitude of the Ukrainian People” intended to recognize foreign nations for solidarity with Ukraine.

“The whole world would go along with that,” said Gates, who met with Xi three years ago, when he was the first foreign entrepreneur to be hosted by the Chinese president post-Covid-19 pandemic.
Gates also said he’d like to propose that countries monitor AI’s ability to create molecules and carry out biological attacks – something that would not get in the way of any tech industry’s development.
Gates’ staff are working to finalise a meeting with Xi for his next China trip, his spokesperson said, scheduled tentatively for November.
President Xi “might be surprised by how vehement I am”, Gates said.
He said China is protecting children from AI companion addiction, but he believes few leaders globally are rising to the occasion to get ahead of a litany of potential harms from AI.
“Yes, in the past, technology never did this. This time is different. This is like an evolutionary milestone that needs incredible policy management by society as a whole.”
AI hacking ‘should blow people’s minds’
Gates struck a more optimistic note about AI in January, but since then he has become concerned that it can conduct attacks while supplanting jobs and hooking users psychologically.
For instance, technology from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta Platforms recently hacked real-world websites in what were supposed to be isolated cybersecurity evaluations.
“These security incidents are shocking, and they should blow people’s minds,” Gates said.
In a blog post on Aug 26, Gates called for a new international organisation to manage AI, drawing on elements from a nuclear inspections regime, international aviation regulations, and ozone layer protection agreements.
To date, US President Donald Trump’s administration has exercised some control over the distribution of powerful AI models such as Anthropic’s Fable 5, but more regulation has taken place at the state level.
Whereas many tech leaders have, like Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, touted the benefits of AI, many have also expressed concern about its perils.
Demis Hassabis, chair of Google DeepMind, proposed a body like the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, or FINRA, that could develop and conduct tests of AI related to national security.
Gates agrees with others that the United States should take the lead, but says it must establish what criteria would determine what action.
“You can use a FINRA-type model, but it’s a silly conversation,” Gates said. “It’s like saying, ‘Should we meet to discuss taxation at this restaurant or this restaurant?’”
‘World’s top priority’
In his blog post, Gates said it was the “world’s top priority” to deliver an AI future that does not widen inequality and hurt the vulnerable, ahead of climate change and health crises.
As he pursues high-profile engagements, Gates also told Reuters he planned to see British Prime Minister Andy Burnham this autumn.
In February, he cancelled an appearance in India after the US released files from sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
Gates has said he did not realise the extent of Epstein’s crimes when associating with him for philanthropy.
His foundation is aiming to spend US$200 billion (S$253.98 billion) by 2045 with an increasing focus on AI.
It is working with Anthropic on AI-powered health checks for pregnancy, and with OpenAI to help healthcare workers in Rwanda, Gates said.
He also will speak to personnel at Anthropic and OpenAI, both of which are preparing blockbuster IPOs, about impactful giving, he said.
On his mind are various ideas for addressing social upheaval.
He envisioned taxing revenue from companies using “tokens” or AI’s outputs to supplant labour, which could help fund a safety net.
He also said society should reserve up to 40 per cent of current jobs for humans, noting in the blog how care his dad received when suffering from Alzheimer’s disease was “irreplaceably human”.
Gates said community protests centred on data centres were missing a bigger picture. “Wait until you really screw up the job market,” he said. REUTERS

vibrant card deck by julia schimautz hides an animation in its sequence of colors and shapes
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
07:45:16 UTC
16:45:16 KST

color, printmaking, and movement converge in color index
Austrian graphic designer and printmaker Julia Schimautz collaborates with Copenhagen-based Small Wonder CPH on Color Index, a deck of playing cards that turns a familiar object into a small kinetic image. Across the cards, saturated fields of color gradually shift and accumulate into oversized suit symbols; when the deck is riffled, the individual frames combine into a moving image that exists only through the user’s interaction with the cards.
At first glance, the deck follows the basic visual grammar of a conventional pack. Letters and numbers identify the cards while hearts, clubs, diamonds, and spades remain recognizable as suits. But instead of relying on the familiar red-and-black palette, Schimautz distributes each suit across a distinct field of saturated color. Subtle changes from one card to the next become more apparent when the pack is viewed as a whole, with gradients and blurred forms accumulating across the individual surfaces. The King card, for example, carries an enlarged suit symbol that appears to emerge from the surrounding color field.
all images courtesy of Small Wonder CPH
the playing card becomes a sequence of color
Schimautz, who runs the Berlin-based DTAN Studio, approaches graphic design through an interest in experimentation, imperfection, and the physical behavior of printed matter. Her practice is particularly informed by printmaking and Riso printing, where shifts in registration and color can become part of the visual language.
The graphic designer’s interest in the imperfections of printing is important to the character of the deck. Her work embraces the small discrepancies that can occur when colors and layers are translated from digital designs into physical prints, allowing the process itself to influence the finished image.
That approach is particularly suited to a deck whose visual identity depends on repetition and incremental change. Each card is recognizable as part of the same system, but the progression between cards creates the larger image. Color, therefore, functions as a structural device, organizing the sequence and controlling how the animation is perceived.
The deck is printed on FSC-certified black-core paper using vegetable-based inks and finished with a linen texture. Its construction keeps the object close to the conventions of a traditional poker deck while giving the surface and edges a more pronounced graphic presence.

Iran seek to end Indian and Chinese Taipei kabaddi dominance
TEHRAN - Iran’s women’s national kabaddi team are entering the 2026 Asian Games with a significantly reshaped squad, as the coaching staff seeks to build a new generation of players capable of challenging the traditional dominance of India and Chinese Taipei.
Speaking about the team’s preparations, the technical adviser of Iran’s women’s national kabaddi team, Gholamreza Mazandarani, said around 78 percent of the squad has changed this year. The new team are considerably younger than previous editions, with many players showing high motivation and energy but lacking experience at the international level.
According to the technical adviser, gaining competitive experience was therefore a major priority from the beginning of the team’s preparation.
“The coaching staff had planned a series of friendly and preparatory matches to expose the young players to international competition. However, the plans were delayed by several obstacles, including the war, flight disruptions, difficulties related to leaving the country and the refusal of some potential host countries to accept the team for friendly matches,” Mazandarani said.
Despite these challenges, the team eventually managed to take part in an international training camp and a series of matches. The technical adviser described the experience as extremely valuable, particularly for the younger members of the squad. For many of the players, it was their first international trip and their first opportunity to compete against foreign opponents.
“The camp also gave the coaching staff an opportunity to assess the players under competitive conditions. Almost every member of the squad was given the chance to play in six or seven full matches, allowing the coaches to evaluate their abilities and determine how they could contribute to the national team,” he added.
The technical adviser acknowledged that transforming a young and inexperienced squad into a genuine championship contender in a limited period would be difficult. He said that simply declaring the gold medal as the team’s objective could be considered somewhat ambitious. Nevertheless, the coaching staff is determined to prepare the team for the best possible performance at the Asian Games.
Iran will face particularly strong competition from India and Chinese Taipei, two teams that have traditionally occupied the top positions in women’s Asian kabaddi. The technical adviser pointed out that both rivals benefit from regularly hosting tournaments and competitions in their own countries. Their players consequently gain continuous match experience and become more mature through frequent exposure to competitive situations.
“Despite the difficult circumstances, Iran hope their new generation can close the experience gap and challenge the established order. The immediate objective is not merely to participate, but to build a competitive team capable of breaking the long-standing India–Chinese Taipei duopoly and fighting for the best possible medal at the Asian Games,” Mazandarani concluded.

U.S. Army seeks new short-range missile similar to JAGM, Hellfire
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
07:39:07 UTC
16:39:07 KST

- The U.S. Army is asking companies whether they can build a new short-range missile similar to JAGM and Hellfire, with production starting by 2028.
- The Army wants 8,000 missiles delivered within two years of any contract, then another 8,000 every year after that.
The U.S. Army wants to know if defense companies can build a new short-range guided missile similar to two weapons already in its arsenal, the Joint Air-to-Ground Missile and the Hellfire, with actual production starting by early 2028. Army Contracting Command at Redstone Arsenal, Alabama, published the request August 25 on behalf of the Army’s missile procurement office.
For now, this is just market research, not an actual order. The Army is asking industry whether anyone out there already has a working missile, ready to build in bulk, that fits what the service needs. It wants a weapon that works in bad weather, can push through electronic jamming that blocks GPS signals, and can dodge modern countermeasures designed to throw missiles off target.
The Army laid out specific numbers: a missile that can hit targets anywhere from about 500 meters to 8 kilometers (5 miles) or farther away, and one that can be fired from helicopters, drones, ground vehicles or boats using a standard launcher. On the target list: tanks and armored vehicles, command posts, enemy air defense radars, small attack boats, and drones.
That last item, drones, is not a hypothetical use case. Missiles from the same Hellfire family the Army is describing are already being used for exactly that job, and not just on paper. Ukraine’s 302nd Anti-Aircraft Missile Brigade recently showed off a homemade air defense system called STASH, built by bolting AGM-114L Longbow Hellfire missiles onto a radar and welding the whole setup onto a military truck.
The Longbow variant carries a radar seeker that lets it lock onto a target on its own after launch, useful against a fast-moving drone. Paired with a compact radar built to spot small, low-flying aircraft, the system gives Ukrainian troops a way to shoot down Shahed-type attack drones without spending a multimillion-dollar Patriot interceptor on a target that might have cost Russia only a few tens of thousands of dollars to build.
The U.S. military has taken notice. In August, the Marine Corps signed an $19 million contract for 10 more Tempest vehicles, a lightweight buggy built by V2X that also carries AGM-114L Longbow Hellfire missiles to hunt down drones. At least two Tempest vehicles have already been fighting in Ukraine, where the Ukrainian Air Force credits the system with destroying 21 Shahed drones.
That combat record made the Tempest an easier sell to the Marine Corps than a system still stuck in testing. Between STASH and Tempest, the same missile the Army is now describing in its new notice, one capable of hitting targets from 500 meters out to several kilometers, has already proven itself doing double duty: killing tanks and killing drones with the same warhead.
The Army’s new notice doesn’t name a specific missile or company, but the requirements closely track the specifications of the AGM-179 Joint Air-to-Ground Missile and the AGM-114 Hellfire, both built by Lockheed Martin. JAGM entered service with the Marine Corps in 2022 and was built to replace three older missile types, Hellfire, Maverick and TOW, with one weapon that can guide itself using either a laser or radar. Each JAGM missile costs roughly $319,000, and the Pentagon has said it eventually wants more than 26,000 of them.
Any company that thinks it can meet the Army’s requirement needs to prove it can gear up fast. The Army wants a contractor ready to start full production by the last quarter of fiscal year 2028, and it wants the first 8,000 missiles, plus spare parts, delivered within two years of any contract being signed. After that, the Army wants another 8,000 missiles delivered every year on a repeating cycle.

Fire at hospital in Pakistan's capital Islamabad kills 14 infants
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
07:39:00 UTC
16:39:00 KST

A fire at a state-run hospital in Pakistan’s capital killed at least 14 infants Wednesday, the prime minister said, with local media blaming a faulty air-conditioning system.
The blaze started around 7 a.m. (2 a.m. GMT) at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), on the third floor of the hospital's mother and child health ward, said broadcaster Geo TV, which put the death toll at 15.
"Give me my child," Javeria, who lost her newborn, said outside the hospital, where ambulances had gathered. "I want justice."
The incident is among the deadliest hospital fires in recent years in the country, where government healthcare is subsidized but facilities are under-resourced and overburdened while watchdogs have frequently criticized state-run facilities as mismanaged.
There were 16 newborns in the ward when the fire broke out, one of whom was rescued, Geo reported. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's office said he had directed authorities to conduct an immediate investigation.
The ward was cordoned off, a Reuters witness said.
Mudasir, another parent who also lost his child, said all doors of the ward, except one, were shut and that there was "no fire security" in the ward. Javeria and Mudasir both gave only their first names.
There was no immediate comment from the hospital or authorities on the incident. PIMS, centrally located in Islamabad where jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan was briefly treated last week, is one of the main public hospitals of the city of around 1.1 million people.

The Trump administration has suspended visa interview appointments worldwide

The Trump administration has suspended visa interview appointments worldwide
Kyiv • UNN
The Trump administration has suspended visa interview appointments for applicants worldwide due to global training for consular staff. Applicants are having their appointments rescheduled, while the policy of tightening immigration faces legal obstacles.
The administration of U.S. President Donald Trump has suspended scheduling visa interviews for applicants from around the world as part of the U.S. government's immigration policy during the Republican leader's second term in the White House, Reuters reports, according to UNN.
Details
A U.S. State Department spokesperson said on Tuesday that a global training initiative had been launched at all U.S. embassies and consulates worldwide, and that visa-service appointments would be adjusted to accommodate the training.
Trump has launched an aggressive deportation and immigration campaign that includes canceling visas and green cards, as well as rejecting applications for a range of reasons, such as political views and pro-Palestinian protests against the U.S. ally Israel's attack on Gaza, the publication writes. He reportedly says the policy is aimed at improving domestic security.
The policy has encountered some legal obstacles. On Friday, a U.S. judge ordered the Trump administration to rescind its policy suspending the issuance of immigrant visas to applicants from 75 countries, stating that the policy exceeded the powers granted by law to Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
The State Department did not provide details about the training or its duration, other than saying that "the training was intended to help consular officers screen out applicants deemed likely to become dependent on U.S. government benefits and ensure a "comprehensive and consistent" assessment of visa applicants.
The suspension of visa interview appointments was previously reported by the Financial Times, which noted that immigrant visa applicants who had interviews scheduled at U.S. embassies and consulates received emails saying that their appointments were being rescheduled and that they would be notified of a new date in the future.
Although Trump campaigned in 2024 on ending illegal immigration, his administration has also made legal immigration more difficult—for example, by introducing new and higher fees for applicants for certain work visas.

Two More Satellites From Russia’s Starlink Alternative Face Atmospheric Reentry
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-26
07:34:39 UTC
16:34:39 KST

- Category
- World
Two More Satellites From Russia’s Starlink Alternative Face Atmospheric Reentry
Russia’s attempt to construct a domestic alternative to SpaceX’s Starlink, aimed at delivering high-speed satellite internet and establishing a dedicated military space communications network, is encountering mounting technical failures in orbit.
At least two satellites deployed during the second mass launch on July 20, 2026, are expected to be lost, according to space researcher Anatoly Zak, as reported by The Moscow Times on August 25.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
Tracking data published by Russian Space Web indicates that these spacecraft failed to perform orbital elevation maneuvers, falling below an altitude of 300 kilometers, and are likely to reenter Earth’s atmosphere, where they will break apart and burn up.
Three additional satellites from the same launch made unsuccessful attempts to raise their orbits and are currently descending, remaining at altitudes between 310 and 330 km.
Nine other spacecraft continue to perform maneuvers, but their altitudes remain roughly 200 km lower than those of the initial deployment phase at the same point in mission operations.
The project, spearheaded by aerospace company Bureau 1440, launched its first batch of 17 satellites in late March. One spacecraft from that initial group failed to reach its target orbit and burned up in early June.
While 14 satellites eventually formed a chain at an altitude slightly above 500 km, none managed to reach the planned operational height of 800 km designated by Bureau 1440.
Astronomer Jonathan McDowell noted ongoing difficulties with raising orbits within the Rassvet-3 constellation, which is designed to provide broadband data transmission globally.
Maintaining spacecraft at a lower 500 km orbit remains technically possible, but increased gravitational drag requires higher fuel consumption to sustain altitude, significantly reducing the operational lifespan of the satellites, Zak explained.
Roscosmos head Dmitry Bakanov previously stated in June 2025 that the first stage of the 430-billion-ruble ($4.7 billion) Rassvet project would feature 350 satellites to provide continuous global coverage, with plans to eventually expand the network to 900 spacecraft.
Moscow intended to begin commercial operation in 2027, with Russian leader Vladimir Putin noting that the system would support military drone command networks.
Before that, Russian forces had relied on unauthorized access to Starlink terminals obtained through third-party supply chains to support battlefield communications and drone operations. Ukraine, in coordination with SpaceX, introduced technical restrictions that disabled a significant portion of these terminals by limiting access to registered users.
The impact on Russian units was immediate, with operations disrupted following the loss of secure communication channels. Ukrainian military sources reported a decline in coordination efficiency, while Ukraine’s Defense Ministry adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov said the restrictions created a “catastrophe” for Russian forces on certain sections of the front.
